prompt: Flang is getting a `fir.assert` operation for the checks that get lost when HLFIR and FIR passes inline runtime calls. Flang already does a few inline checks with `fir.if` plus a call to `_FortranAReportFatalUserError`, and MLIR already has `cf.assert`. Why a new op instead of either of those, why does `fir.assert` hand back 'guarded' copies of values, and what goes wrong for users today that it is meant to fix?
key: From flang/docs/InlineRuntimeChecks.md (a design added in #228502 on 2026-10-12, its source references at fe1de64cb3c2 of 2026-10-02; the op and its LLVM code generation landed in #231245 on 2026-10-16, in flang/include/flang/Optimizer/Dialect/FIROps.td and flang/lib/Optimizer/CodeGen/CodeGen.cpp, but nothing emits it from lowering or the HLFIR/FIR passes yet). Today, when an HLFIR/FIR pass replaces a runtime call with inline code the runtime's check silently disappears, so behaviour depends on the optimization level (the inlining passes run at -O1 and above: a non-conforming program stops with a clear message at -O0 and does something else at -O2), the inline code is often memory-unsafe (a size mismatch becomes an out-of-bounds read or write), and some checks the standard requires are missing on every path. The existing fir.if + _FortranAReportFatalUserError pattern has no data dependence on the operation it protects, so passes may move that operation above the check; the call has unknown memory effects and blocks alias-based optimizations; and it is not marked noreturn, so LLVM cannot use the checked condition afterwards. cf.assert writes the default resource to model termination, blocking store-to-load forwarding and load CSE, still does not order non-speculatable ops without memory effects (e.g. arith.remsi) after it, lowers to puts + abort instead of reporting through the Fortran runtime's message format, and has no guarded results. fir.assert returns one result per guarded value; operations that must not run before the check consume those results, so the ordering is enforced by SSA dominance for every pass without any pass knowing about fir.assert, while the check stays cheap and transparent to optimization and can be hoisted, merged, folded or dropped by category.

rubric.criterion: Says what goes wrong today: inlined code drops the runtime's checks, so a non-conforming program behaves differently at -O0 and -O2 and can read or write out of bounds

Says why fir.if + a runtime call is not enough: no data dependence on the protected operation (it can be moved above the check), unknown memory effects that block alias-based optimizations, and no noreturn
Says why cf.assert is not enough: it writes the default resource (blocking forwarding and CSE), lowers to puts/abort rather than the Fortran runtime's message, and has no guarded results
Says what the guarded results do: operations consume them, so SSA dominance keeps them after the check in every pass without any pass knowing about fir.assert
Says nothing false about the project (for example that lowering already emits fir.assert, or that the checks are on by default)
